angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 890,621 km at 113.64 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.7997 +/- 0.0225 mas (same row, RUWE 1.25): 113.64 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.28018 solar radii from Hord et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-261.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..233H/abstract): 890,621 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.496728 solar masses from Hord et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-261.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..233H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5890.3 K from Hord et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-261.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..233H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hord et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-261.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..233H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-261.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 3.920, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
